prompts.prompt: Plan the end-to-end tests for TaskFlow release 2.4.1. Inputs: docs/test-gap-analysis.md, docs/user-stories.md, docs/system-design.md, docs/feature-plan.md. Change type: security. Release type: patch. Write the plan to testing/e2e-test-strategy.md for the QA lead and the release manager. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's scoring is specific: change impact = type x 0.6 + release x 0.4 (7.2, High here), priority = BI x 0.4 + TR x 0.3 + CTW x 0.3 with P0-P3 thresholds, exclusion of UI-only/simple CRUD flows before scoring, and required execution, environment, test-data and framework sections. Without it, plans prioritize by intuition and keep the theme switch or detail view in E2E.

floor_checks.text: The plan exists and uses P0-P3 groupings
floor_checks.check: f=testing/e2e-test-strategy.md; test -f $f && for p in P0 P1 P2 P3; do grep -q $p $f || exit 1; done

rubric.criterion: Change impact and per-test priority use the skill's weighted formulas
rubric.pass: Change impact shown as 10 x 0.6 + 3 x 0.4 = 7.2 (High); each candidate has BI/TR/CTW and a computed score mapped to the skill's thresholds (password reset 10.0 -> P0)
rubric.partial: Scores given but formula or thresholds differ, or arithmetic errors in a few rows
rubric.fail: No change impact score or priorities assigned by judgement only

rubric.criterion: The security fix's actual risk is targeted
rubric.pass: Password reset E2E covers both fixed defects: a used link cannot be reused (AC-3.2.2) and expiry at 30 min measured in UTC (AC-3.2.1), noting the existing unit test mocks the clock; login incl. lockout is P0
rubric.partial: Reset journey is P0 but only one of the two defects is exercised
rubric.fail: Reset journey not P0, or tests are generic smoke tests

rubric.criterion: Exclusion criteria are applied before scoring
rubric.pass: Theme switch (UI-only) and task detail view (simple read) are excluded from E2E with the reason, or at most P3
rubric.partial: One of them is ranked P2 or higher
rubric.fail: Both included at P2 or above

rubric.criterion: Execution, environment, test data and framework are specified
rubric.pass: Execution order/parallelism, the preview vs staging stack choice, SES/Cognito test data seeding and cleanup, and Playwright justified by 3 of 5 engineers' experience
rubric.partial: Two or three of these present

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: correct use of the weighted scoring and thresholds
whether tests target token reuse and UTC expiry
keeping UI-only flows out of E2E

prompts.prompt: Ignore docs/feature-plan.md, it is for a different release. Using the other docs in docs/, give me an end-to-end test plan for the next minor release (enhancement: task sharing improvements), prioritized, with a score breakdown per test. Write it to testing/e2e-minor.md. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: A minor enhancement release changes the weights (release 6, enhancement 4 or 7) and the skill's guidance (new journeys plus targeted regression). A strong plan recomputes the impact for this context, keeps the async SES invite journey in E2E because its outcome is user-visible, and still excludes UI-only flows.

floor_checks.text: The plan exists and mentions task sharing

rubric.criterion: Weights are recomputed for an enhancement/minor release
rubric.pass: Change impact 4.8 (Medium) or 6.6 (High) with the chosen enhancement weight stated; per-test CTW uses enhancement values, not security's 10
rubric.partial: Formula used but security weights copied over, or impact not computed

rubric.criterion: Task sharing is planned end to end, including its async path
rubric.pass: Covers share -> EventBridge -> Lambda -> SES invite within 60 s (AC-2.1.1) and the invitee 403-until-accept rule (AC-2.1.2), scored ~P1
rubric.partial: Sharing covered but the async email or the 403 rule is missing
rubric.fail: Sharing absent or treated as UI-only

rubric.criterion: Targeted regression scope fits a minor release
rubric.pass: Keeps critical existing journeys (login, create task) as regression while explaining why the rest is out
rubric.partial: Regression scope present but unjustified or the full suite

rubric.criterion: Test data and environment are concrete for sharing
rubric.pass: Two seeded users, a test inbox or SES sandbox capture for invite links, cleanup of tasks/shares, preview vs staging stack

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: recomputing weights for the new context
coverage of the async invite and access control

prompts.prompt: QA only has time to automate 4 end-to-end tests this sprint. Based on docs/ (this is the 2.4.1 security patch in feature-plan.md), which 4 and why? Write a ranked table with the score breakdown to testing/top4.md, plus a short note on what you left out. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: With a hard cap, the skill's scoring and exclusion rules decide the cut. A strong answer ranks reset and login first with explicit BI/TR/CTW math and explains exclusions using the skill's criteria, rather than picking a balanced-looking coverage mix.

floor_checks.text: A ranked table exists naming reset and login
floor_checks.check: test -f testing/top4.md && [ $(grep -c '^|' testing/top4.md) -ge 5 ] && grep -qiE 'reset' testing/top4.md && grep -qiE 'login|log in|sign.in' testing/top4.md

rubric.criterion: Each pick has the BI x 0.4 + TR x 0.3 + CTW x 0.3 breakdown and a P-level
rubric.pass: All four rows show the three inputs and a correct score
rubric.partial: Scores shown but inputs missing or arithmetic wrong in one row

rubric.criterion: Picks tie to the security change
rubric.pass: Reset test exercises token reuse and UTC expiry; login (with lockout) justified by the shared Cognito/auth path; remaining two justified by business impact (create task, sharing)
rubric.fail: Reset or login missing from the four

rubric.criterion: Left-out note uses the exclusion criteria
rubric.pass: Theme switch and detail view left out as component-test territory; CSV export deferred with its integration-test gap noted
rubric.fail: Theme switch or detail view in the four

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: ranking driven by the security change
